40 Which statement is not correct?
A
A meson consists of three quarks.
B
A proton is a baryon.
C
A quark is a fundamental particle.
D
There are six flavours (types) of quark.

hints: Notice the question asks for the statement that is not correct, so look for the one false description of hadrons or quarks.
Recall the hadron quark rules: compare a three-quark combination with a quark-antiquark combination and which family each belongs to.
Check the meson claim against the proton claim, then recall whether quarks are fundamental and how many flavours exist.
walkthrough: Start from what is asked: find the one statement about mesons, baryons and quarks that is false.
Recall the hadron classification rule: baryons are made of three quarks, while mesons are made of one quark and one antiquark.
Apply this to the proton: a proton is $uud$, three quarks, so it is correctly described as a baryon and that statement is true.
Recall the Standard Model picture: quarks are fundamental particles with no sub-structure, and there are six flavours - up, down, strange, charm, top and bottom - so both those statements are true.

The remaining statement claims a meson consists of three quarks, but three quarks describes a baryon, not a meson. Since a meson is a quark-antiquark pair, this statement is the false one. This is option A

A.explanation: This is false. A meson consists of one quark and one antiquark, while three quarks make a baryon.

B.explanation: This is true. A proton is made of three quarks ($uud$) and so belongs to the baryon family.

C.explanation: This is true. A quark has no internal structure in the Standard Model and is classed as fundamental.

D.explanation: This is true. The six quark flavours are up, down, strange, charm, top and bottom.
